claims.text: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a single-phase refractory BCC alloy.
The proposed intervention produces Hf0.8V0.2MoTaTiZr by partially replacing Hf with V.
The Hf-to-V substitution will reduce density by 5–10% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will retain a room-temperature yield strength of at least approximately 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain a yield strength of at least approximately 850 MPa at 1000 °C.
Replacing Hf with lighter V lowers average atomic mass and thereby lowers the alloy's mass per unit volume.
The modified alloy will remain a single-phase refractory BCC solid solution.
Vanadium substitution will cause only a slight modification of lattice parameters and atomic packing.
Preservation of the BCC matrix will help preserve high-temperature strength.
Solid-solution strengthening will be preserved after the Hf-to-V substitution.
Residual lattice distortion will remain sufficient to hinder dislocation motion.
The retained lattice distortion and BCC structure will maintain yield strength and ductility at room temperature and 1000 °C.
Ductility and other mechanical properties will remain similar to the baseline if phase stability is maintained.
Mechanical evaluation is limited to room temperature and 1000 ± 50 °C under quasi-static loading at approximately 10⁻³ s⁻¹.
Vanadium substitution may adversely affect high-temperature phase stability or microstructural homogeneity.
The hypothesis is rejected if density reduction is below 5%, room-temperature yield strength is below approximately 1440 MPa, or high-temperature yield strength is below approximately 765 MPa.

contradictions.description: The wording 'replacing approximately 20 at.% of Hf' can mean replacing 20 percentage points of the entire equiatomic alloy, whereas Hf0.8V0.2MoTaTiZr corresponds to replacing only 20% of the original Hf inventory: normalized composition is 16 at.% Hf and 4 at.% V.

The hypothesis predicts preservation near 1600 MPa at room temperature and at least 850 MPa at 1000 °C, but the rejection rule permits strengths as low as 1440 and 765 MPa. Results below the stated predicted strengths could therefore fail the central 'without sacrificing' prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under its rule.
